title: Merry and Puddle's Wobbly Race
markdown:
In Cloverpatch Village lived two of the most fun-loving critters around: Merry the bunny and Puddle the duck.

Merry loved to hop. He could hop over a dandelion, hop under a daisy, and sometimes, if he wasn’t watching, hop right over his own twitchy tail. His whiskers jiggled with glee at the thought of a good hop. His biggest dream was to win the super-duper, wiggle-your-ears-off Grand Hop at Village Sports Day. Every morning, BOING, BOING, BOING, he practised, fluffy white tail a happy blur. He imagined the sparkly blue ribbon and everyone shouting that Merry was the fastest hopper ever.

Puddle loved to paddle. Splish, splash, quack. He could make little waves even in a teacup. His bright eyes sparkled like dewdrops when he thought of gliding. He loved Sports Day too, especially the Speedy Swim. He practised smooth swooshing strokes in the babbling brook by his nest, webbed feet going swish-swish-swish. He imagined cool water, spray on his feathers, and everyone cheering that Puddle was the fastest swimmer ever.

Village Sports Day was a huge deal, the most exciting event of the year. There were races for running, jumping, swimming, and even rolling acorns. The air buzzed like a hive of happy bees, and everyone brought picnic baskets overflowing with carrot cakes and sweet berry tarts. This year, oh boy, there was a brand-new event: a super-duper, never-before-seen, head-scratching challenge called the Hop and Paddle Challenge. You had to race as a team of two. One hopped. The other paddled. It sounded fantastically exciting, and maybe, just maybe, a tiny bit tricky. It was a chance for all sorts of animals to work together, which was a totally new and interesting idea.

“Merry,” quacked Puddle, wobbling up to Merry’s burrow one sunny morning. Merry was practising a spectacular hop over his garden gnome. “Have you heard? The Hop and Paddle Challenge. We should totally be a team.”

Merry’s ears shot up. “A team? With you, Puddle? That would be absolutely, wonderfully marvellous. I’ll do all the hopping, and you can do all the paddling.” He did a little happy bounce. Boing.

Puddle blinked, head tilting. “But Merry. The rules say one of us has to hop, and the other has to paddle. If we’re a team, and I paddle, then you have to hop. And if you hop, then I have to paddle.”

Merry’s whiskers drooped. Oh. Right. He hadn’t quite thought of that. Ears flopped. “Oh. Right. But you’re a duck. You’re born to paddle. You glide like a whisper. And I’m a bunny. I’m born to hop. I can jump over the moon if I really try.”

“Hmm,” Puddle mused, looking at the fluffy clouds. “Maybe we can teach each other?”

Merry giggled, bubbly. “Teach you to hop? You’re a duck. You’re all wibbly-wobbly when you walk. You look like a funny little dance. And teach me to paddle? I’d sink like a stone. A little bunny submarine.”

That was the start of their great training adventure. Interesting. Maybe a little messy.

They started with Merry teaching Puddle to hop, on a nice flat patch of meadow. “Okay, Puddle. You just bend your knees like this, and then PUSH. Whoosh.” Merry sprang, a perfect fluffy arc against the blue.

Puddle wobbled his knees. He bent them. He wiggled them. He pushed… and did a little flop onto his tummy with a soft oof. “Quack. That’s not hopping. That’s belly-flopping.” He looked up, a smear of green on his beak.

Merry chuckled, warm and rumbly. “It’s okay. You almost got it. You need more bounce. Like a spring.” Another mighty leap over buttercups. Puddle tried again. Bent. Wiggled. Pushed. He sort of shuffled forward, wings flapping wildly for balance, like catching a runaway kite. Less hopping, more a confused goose doing a jig. “Quack. I think I’m just waddling with enthusiasm.” Merry’s nose twitched with amusement.

Then Puddle taught Merry to paddle, at the sparkling pond. “Alright, Merry.” Puddle slipped in, at home as if wearing his favourite swimming costume. “It’s all in the feet. Little circles, like this.” Webbed feet made tiny elegant whirlwinds.

Merry dipped a paw. “Ooh, cold. And a bit slippery.” He tried circles. His paws were too fluffy and round. They swished and sloshed. He didn’t move forward. He bobbed like a cork. Then he tried to kick. Splash. Water everywhere. He still didn’t move. He floated on his back, looking at clouds. “I think I’m just a floating bunny.”

Puddle paddled over, shaking droplets. “Oh, Merry. Maybe hopping and paddling aren’t the easiest things to teach.” A little sad. Merry’s whiskers drooped again, ears touching his paws. “Maybe we should just stick to what we’re good at,” he murmured. “You swim the Speedy Swim. I’ll win the Grand Hop. That’s what we’re meant to do.”

Other villagers began to notice. Tegwen the badger, who always had a chuckle for everyone’s efforts, saw Merry flopping around trying to paddle and Puddle splashing without moving. “Hah,” he chuckled, leaning on his walking stick. “A hopping duck and a swimming bunny. They’ll never win that fancy race. What a silly pair.” Mildred the mole popped her head from a tunnel and giggled, tiny nose twitching. Merry and Puddle heard. Ears felt heavy. Tails drooped. They felt a bit wobbly inside, like too many wobbly jellybeans. Not a good feeling.

The day before the race they sat by the pond, glum. Water less sparkly. Sun less warm. Merry’s whiskers almost touched his paws. Puddle let out a long sad sigh like a balloon losing air. “We’re no good at teaching, are we?” Merry whispered, kicking a pebble. “I can’t paddle, and you can’t hop. We’re just not good at being each other.”

“And everyone’s laughing,” Puddle added softly, eyes on his webbed feet. Their Sports Day dreams felt washed away.

Then Merry looked at Puddle. Puddle looked at Merry. Puddle remembered something important. “Wait, Merry.” A spark in his eyes. A tiny flap. “Remember why we wanted to do this? It’s Sports Day. It’s about having fun. And we wanted to do it together.”

Merry’s ears perked a tiny bit. “Together?”

“Yes.” Puddle flapped with a little more energy. “We might not be the best hoppers or paddlers at each other’s sports, but we’re the best Merry and Puddle. We can try. We can help each other. We can be a team, even if we’re a bit silly doing it.”

Just like that, spirits lifted like bubbles. They would not worry about being perfect. They would hop and paddle with all their might, and laugh all the way.

Hop, hop, wobble, paddle.

The next day the whistle blew, sharp and clear. Merry took off with a mighty hop toward the water’s edge, a furry blur. Puddle was already waiting. Merry climbed carefully onto Puddle’s back. “Paddle, Puddle, paddle,” he cheered.

Puddle paddled with all his might. Not the fastest, but steady and strong. Merry, from his perch, tried to help with little bunny hops. Hop, hop, wobble, paddle. It looked absolutely ridiculous, a fluffy toy bouncing on a moving boat, but they were both giggling. Laughter echoed across the water.

When it was time for Merry to hop, Puddle slid him off and Merry bounded with all his bunny power. He’d learned a little wobbly hop when tired, a bit like Puddle’s enthusiastic shuffle. When Puddle needed to paddle, Merry still tried little swishing motions with his paws, cheering with all his might. No paddling medals. Best bunny effort.

They weren’t winning. Oh no, definitely not winning. They were somewhere in the middle, but they were having the most fun. They tumbled into the water at the same time, giggling as they splashed. They helped each other navigate tricky reeds that tried to tickle them. And at one point they even did a synchronized wobbly dance on a big green lily pad. Quite a sight. A frog applauded by not moving, which for a frog is high praise. Hop, hop, wobble, paddle: they said it under their breath like a secret song, and the water seemed to keep time.

The finish line was close. “Let’s go, Puddle,” Merry shouted, bouncing on Puddle’s back. Puddle’s little legs a blur. Merry’s bestest bounciest hops, ears flying. They crossed, not first, not second, not even third, but with the biggest brightest smiles.

The crowd cheered, not for speed, but for spirit. They had tried, laughed until their sides hurt, and won something better than a medal: a shared adventure. Merry wiggled his whiskers, tail a happy flag. Puddle gave a proud happy quack. Hop, hop, wobble, paddle: that was their song all the way home, carrot cake waiting, and nobody asking who came first.
